boards.title: Alert handler
boards.description: The alert-handler webhook receiver: webhooks and alerts received, rule matches, actions by rule, type and result with their duration, and the loaded configuration.

boards.title: Alertmanager
boards.description: Prometheus Alertmanager self-monitoring: alerts received and active, notifications per integration with failures and latency, silences, the gossip cluster and configuration reloads.

boards.title: Grafana
boards.description: Grafana as a service, wherever it runs: its pods, their resources and logs first, then its own metrics, then only the platform tabs that have data (Kubernetes, containers, Docker, systemd, process, ingress, Windows, logs, the Backstage catalog entry), alerts and Kubernetes event annotations.

boards.title: Anomaly / Detector scores
boards.description: The anomaly exporter itself: probes per module, success and failure rates, probe duration and version. Anomaly scores live on the Anomaly scorer board.

boards.title: Anomaly / Process
boards.description: Every series below is compared with its own past: the rolling mean over 1d and a band 3 standard deviations wide. It owns no metrics - point it at any service.

boards.title: Anomaly / Requests
boards.description: Every series below is compared with its own past: the rolling mean over 1d and a band 3 standard deviations wide. It owns no metrics - point it at any service.

boards.title: Burn rate / Kubernetes API server
boards.description: How fast the error budget is being spent, and what that means for the objective. The kube-apiserver-burnrate.rules of kubernetes.cluster (or of the kubernetes-mixin) record these seven windows for the API server's own SLO, split by read and write.

boards.title: Burn rate / Pyrra SLOs
boards.description: How fast the error budget is being spent, and what that means for the objective. Pyrra publishes the availability and the objective per SLO; the burn and the budget left follow from the two.

boards.title: Capacity / Certificates
boards.description: When this runs out, at the rate of the last 6h. Seconds until each cert-manager certificate expires. This one shrinks by a second per second, so the prediction is exact rather than a trend.

boards.title: Capacity / Cluster CPU
boards.description: How full this is, how full it was 7d ago, and where the trend of the last 6h puts it in 4d. Cores in use against cores available, per cluster. Under 30 percent says the cluster is paid for and idle; over 70 says the next node is already late.

boards.title: Capacity / Cluster memory
boards.description: How full this is, how full it was 7d ago, and where the trend of the last 6h puts it in 4d. Memory in use against memory installed, per cluster.

boards.title: Capacity / Filesystems
boards.description: When this runs out, at the rate of the last 6h. Free bytes per mounted filesystem, minus the ones that live in memory and cannot fill up the way a disk does.

boards.title: Capacity / Free node memory
boards.description: When this runs out, at the rate of the last 6h. Memory the kernel says is available - which is not free memory, it counts what the cache would give back.

boards.title: Capacity / Node CPU
boards.description: How full this is, how full it was 7d ago, and where the trend of the last 6h puts it in 4d. The same question per node, which is where the imbalance shows: a cluster at 50 percent can still have a node at 95.

boards.title: Capacity / Node memory
boards.description: How full this is, how full it was 7d ago, and where the trend of the last 6h puts it in 4d. Memory in use against memory installed, per node.

boards.title: Capacity / Workload memory
boards.description: How full this is, how full it was 7d ago, and where the trend of the last 6h puts it in 4d. What each namespace uses against what it is allowed. Over 100 percent means it has no limits set, not that it is overcommitted.

boards.title: Alloy
boards.description: Alloy as a service, wherever it runs: its pods, their resources and logs first, then its own metrics, then only the platform tabs that have data (Kubernetes, containers, Docker, systemd, process, ingress, Windows, logs, the Backstage catalog entry), alerts and Kubernetes event annotations.

boards.title: Anomaly exporter
boards.description: The anomaly exporter itself: probes per module, success and failure rates, probe duration and version. Anomaly scores live on the Anomaly scorer board.

boards.title: Blackbox exporter
boards.description: Black-box probes from blackbox_exporter: availability and uptime per target, probe latency by phase (HTTP, ICMP, DNS), HTTP status, version and redirects, TLS certificate expiry and version, and the exporter itself. A row is one target (instance) probed by one module (job).

boards.title: Node exporter
boards.description: node_exporter reporting on itself: the collectors it ran, what each cost, and whether the scrape completed. When a Linux board has holes in it, the reason is here.

boards.title: OpenCost
boards.description: Kubernetes cost from OpenCost: node hourly cost, allocation per namespace priced with the node rates, persistent volumes, spot nodes, egress and the cluster management fee. Monthly figures assume 730 hours.

boards.title: Pushgateway
boards.description: Prometheus Pushgateway: the groups batch jobs push and how long ago each last succeeded or failed, stale groups, push traffic (rate, errors, duration, size) and the gateway process. Groups are filtered with **Pushed job**, the gateway itself with **Job** / **Instance**.

boards.title: kube-state-metrics
boards.description: kube-state-metrics' own health from its telemetry endpoint: list and watch outcomes per resource, sharding, and the process.

boards.title: Linux node
boards.description: One Linux host from node_exporter: facts and health tiles, then CPU, memory, disk, network, temperature and pressure rows, plus exporter tabs that appear only where their metrics exist (Proxmox, Docker, kubelet, Batocera, ZFS, NFS, battery, services, updates, logs).

boards.title: Windows node
boards.description: Runtime signals for every instance matching the selected job.

boards.title: Argo CD
boards.description: Argo CD from its own metrics: application health and sync status, sync operations and failures, reconcile latency, cluster and repository connectivity, Kubernetes API and git request traffic, controller workqueues.

boards.title: Backstage
boards.description: The Backstage software catalog read through the Infinity datasource: components with owner, lifecycle, type and system; systems; APIs.

boards.description: Container resource usage from cAdvisor for Kubernetes pods: CPU with throttling, memory against limits, disk IO.

boards.title: Kubernetes pod
boards.description: Runtime signals for every instance matching the selected job.

boards.title: Process group
boards.description: Process groups from process-exporter: CPU, memory, processes and threads, file descriptors, IO and page faults per group and host, top-N tables and scrape health.

boards.title: Systemd unit
boards.description: systemd units from node_exporter: unit state over time, active and failed counts, failed units, restarts and the overall system state.

boards.title: Windows service
boards.description: Windows services from the windows_exporter service collector: what each one is doing, how many run, and the ones set to start automatically that are stopped.

boards.title: Golden signals / Container
boards.description: The four golden signals: latency, traffic, errors and the one RED leaves out, saturation. Saturation is memory against the limit the container was given: the number that decides whether it is about to be killed.

boards.title: Golden signals / Ingress NGINX
boards.description: The four golden signals: latency, traffic, errors and the one RED leaves out, saturation. Saturation is the share of configured upstream connections in use, so it rises before the latency does.

boards.title: Golden signals / Kubernetes API server
boards.description: The four golden signals: latency, traffic, errors and the one RED leaves out, saturation. Saturation here is the flowcontrol queue: requests waiting for a seat, which is what the API server does instead of failing when it is full.

boards.title: Golden signals / Linux node
boards.description: The four golden signals: latency, traffic, errors and the one RED leaves out, saturation. Traffic and errors come from the network, saturation from load against the CPUs it has - the number that leads the rest.

boards.title: NGINX
boards.description: Every NGINX in one place: servers read through nginx-prometheus-exporter (stub status) and ingress-nginx controllers (their own metrics). The Overview lists both kinds; the Server tab shows requests and connections from whichever source a target has, and the Ingress traffic / Controller tabs appear only where an ingress-nginx controller is scraped.

boards.title: Container resources
boards.description: Container resource usage from cAdvisor for Kubernetes pods: CPU with throttling, memory against limits, disk IO.

boards.title: CoreDNS
boards.description: CoreDNS from its Prometheus plugin: requests, responses and rcodes, latency, cache, and server health per pod.

boards.title: Kubernetes cluster
boards.description: Runtime signals for every instance matching the selected job.

boards.title: Kubernetes clusters
boards.description: Every Kubernetes cluster that reports kube-state-metrics, side by side: how many nodes and pods each runs, what they are using, and what is restarting. A hand-port of the kubernetes-mixin multi-cluster board onto signals, so the numbers match what the mixin computes.

boards.title: Kubernetes pod
boards.description: Runtime signals for every instance matching the selected job.

boards.title: cert-manager
boards.description: cert-manager from its controller metrics: certificate readiness and expiry, ClusterIssuer readiness, ACME client requests and controller sync.

boards.title: RED / Django
boards.description: The RED method over django. django-prometheus: responses by status, latency by view and method.

boards.title: RED / Grafana
boards.description: The RED method over grafana. Grafana's own HTTP handlers.

boards.title: RED / HTTP server (OpenTelemetry)
boards.description: The RED method over http server (opentelemetry). OpenTelemetry HTTP server semantic conventions: one histogram per request, split by route and status code.

boards.title: RED / HTTP server (Prometheus client)
boards.description: The RED method over http server (prometheus client). The `http_requests_total` / `http_request_duration_seconds` pair the Prometheus client libraries expose.

boards.title: RED / Ingress NGINX
boards.description: The RED method over ingress nginx. Every request the cluster ingress terminates, as the controller counts them.

boards.title: RED / Kong
boards.description: The RED method over kong. Every request the Kong gateway proxied, as its Prometheus plugin counts them. Point it at http_server_request_duration_seconds_* instead for a Kong exporting OpenTelemetry.

boards.title: RED / Kubernetes API server
boards.description: The RED method over kubernetes api server. Every call to the API server, by resource and verb.

boards.title: RED / Service graph (from traces)
boards.description: The RED method over service graph (from traces). Tempo's metrics-generator, counting every edge between two traced services.

boards.title: .NET
boards.description: The .NET runtime as exposed by prometheus-net: managed heap, thread pool, exceptions and JIT activity.

boards.title: Django
boards.description: A Django application as django-prometheus reports it: requests by view and method, responses by status, latency measured inside and around the middleware stack, and exceptions by view and type.

boards.title: Go
boards.description: The Go runtime as exposed by `client_golang`: goroutines, threads, heap, stack and garbage collection, plus the shared `process_*` metrics.

boards.title: JVM
boards.description: JVM memory pools, threads, loaded classes and garbage collection, as exposed by Micrometer or the JMX exporter.

boards.title: Node.js
boards.description: The Node.js event loop, V8 heap and handle/request counts, as exposed by `prom-client` default metrics.

boards.title: Python
boards.description: CPython garbage collection plus the process metrics exposed by `prometheus_client` default collectors.

boards.title: Rails
boards.description: A Rails application as yabeda-rails reports it: requests by controller action and status, request duration percentiles, and the split of that time between the database, view rendering and outbound service calls.

boards.title: Rust
boards.description: The Tokio runtime as exposed by the `tokio-metrics` crate: the worker threads, what they are busy with, and the queues behind them. Rust has no runtime of its own to measure, so this is the async executor most services run on.
